nodes.name: Jensen-Grotberg thin film system with insoluble surfactant
nodes.statement_short: Coupled lubrication-approximation evolution equations for film height $h$ and surfactant concentration $\Gamma$ (gravity, capillarity, van der Waals, Marangoni).

nodes.name: Film height equation (1a)
nodes.statement:
{2}
		\partial_t h &=-\partial_x \left[ \frac{h^2}{2}\partial_x \sigma(\Gamma)-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}h^3\partial_x h + \frac{\mathcal{S}}{3}h^3\partial_x^3h+\mathcal{A}\frac{\partial_x h}{h} \right]\; && \mbox{in}\quad \Omega_T

nodes.name: Surfactant concentration equation (1b)
nodes.statement: \partial_t \Gamma &=- \partial_x \left[\Gamma \left(h \partial_x \sigma(\Gamma)-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2} h^2 \partial_x h +\frac{\mathcal{S}}{2} h^2 \partial_x^3 h + \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2} \frac{\partial_x h }{h^{2}}\right)-\mathcal{D}\partial_x \Gamma \right]\;\qquad&&  \mbox{in}\quad \Omega_T.

nodes.name: Time-space domain $\Omega_T$
nodes.statement: Here, $\Omega_T:=(0,T)\times \Omega$ denotes the time-space domain for the unknown functions $h$ and $\Gamma$, with $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}$ being an open, bounded interval.

nodes.name: Initial and boundary conditions for the thin film system
nodes.statement:
The system \eqref{eq:system} is supplemented with initial conditions
\[
h(0,x)=h_0(x)\quad \mbox{and}\quad \Gamma(0,x)=\Gamma_0(x)\qquad \mbox{for all} \quad x\in \Omega,
\]
where $h_0$ and $\Gamma_0$ are given functions and boundary conditions
$$
	\partial_x h =\partial_x \Gamma=0, \quad \mathcal{S}\partial_x^3 f =0 \qquad \mbox{for all}\quad x\in \partial \Omega.
$$

nodes.name: Physical parameters G, S, A, D
nodes.statement: The appearing parameters represent a modified gravitational constant ($\mathcal{G}$), surface tension coefficient ($\mathcal{S}$), Hamaker constant ($\mathcal{A}$), which corresponds to the effects of van der Waals forces, and surface diffusion coefficient ($\mathcal{D}$).

nodes.name: Surface tension equation of state $\sigma$
nodes.statement: Moreover, $\sigma$ is the constitutive equation of state relating the surface tension to the surfactant concentration.
differentia: relating the surface tension to the surfactant concentration

nodes.name: Surface tension positive and nonincreasing
nodes.statement: As the presence of surfactant reduces surface tension, $\sigma$ is assumed to be positive and nonincreasing.

nodes.name: Equation of state $\sigma_\beta$
nodes.statement:
A commonly used description for the dependence of the surface tension on the surfactant is given by  (cf.  \cite{sheludko1967thin,BG,GG})
\[
\sigma_\beta (s):= (\beta +1) \left[1-s+\left(\frac{\beta +1}{\beta}\right)^\frac{1}{3}s\right]^{-3}-\beta, \qquad s\in[0,1]
\]
for $\beta \in (0,\infty)$.

nodes.name: Linear equation of state $\sigma(s)=1-s$
nodes.statement:
For simplicity reasons, in the present work, we assume that $\sigma$ is given by the limit for $\beta\to  \infty$ in $\sigma_\beta$, that is
$$
\sigma (s)= 1-s, \qquad s\in[0,1].
$$
also_stated_at: In what follows we assume that $\sigma(s)=1-s$.

nodes.name: Initial surfactant concentration bounded by 1
nodes.statement: Consequently, it is natural to assume that the initial surfactant concentration $\Gamma_0$ satisfies $0\leq \Gamma_0\leq 1$.

nodes.name: Gravity driven film and capillary driven film
nodes.statement: In our considerations, we are going to consider both cases: The gravity driven film ($\mathcal{S}=0$) and the capillary driven film $(\mathcal{S}>0)$.

nodes.name: Global weak solutions for thin film equations with insoluble surfactant (prior work)
nodes.statement: The existence of nonnegative global weak solutions for the thin film equation with insoluble surfactant was proved by Escher, Hillairet, Lauren{\c{c}}ot \& Walker \cite{EHLW11} for the gravity driven thin film  ($\mathcal S=\mathcal A=0$), and \cite{EHLW4th} for the corresponding capillary driven film ($\mathcal G=\mathcal A=0$) and by Bruell \cite{B2} for the two-phase thin film equation with insoluble surfactant under the influence of capillary forces (see also \cite{GW06, CT13}).
assumptions: for the gravity driven thin film  ($\mathcal S=\mathcal A=0$)
conclusions: The existence of nonnegative global weak solutions for the thin film equation with insoluble surfactant

nodes.name: Torus $\mathbb T$
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathbb T}:=[-\pi,\pi)$.

nodes.name: Sobolev spaces $W^{n,p}(\mathbb T)$
Sobolev space definition
nodes.statement:
W^{n,p}({\mathbb T})=\left\{u\in L^p({\mathbb T})\text{ such that } \|u\|_{W^{n,p}({\mathbb T})}^p:= \|u\|_{L^p}^p+\|\partial_x^n u\|_{L^p}^p<\infty
\right\}
nodes.label: Sobinhomo2

nodes.name: Fourier coefficients and Fourier series
nodes.statement:
We recall the expression of the $k-$th Fourier coefficient and the Fourier series of a $2\pi-$periodic integrable function $u$,
$$
\hat{u}(k)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{{\mathbb T}}u(x)e^{-ix k}dx,\;u(x)=\sum_{k\in{\mathbb Z}}\hat{u}(k)e^{ix k}.
$$

nodes.name: Wiener spaces $\dot A^s(\mathbb T)$
Wiener space definition
nodes.statement: \dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})=\left\{u\in L^1({\mathbb T})\text{ such that } \|u\|_{\dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})}:=\sum_{k\in{\mathbb Z}} |k|^s|\hat{u}(k)| < \infty\right\}.
nodes.label: Wienerinhomo

nodes.name: Wiener algebra is a Banach algebra; Wiener spaces form a Banach scale
nodes.statement: We note that $\dot{A}^0({\mathbb T})=A({\mathbb T})$ is a Banach algebra and $\{\dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})\mid s\geq 0\}$ form a Banach scale.
conclusions: $\dot{A}^0({\mathbb T})=A({\mathbb T})$ is a Banach algebra
$\{\dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})\mid s\geq 0\}$ form a Banach scale

nodes.name: Poincare-like inequality in Wiener spaces
conclusions: \|f\|_{ \dot A^q }\leq \|f\|_{ \dot A^p} \text{ for all } f\in  \dot A^p({\mathbb T}).

nodes.name: Poincare-like inequality (lem:P)
nodes.statement: \|f\|_{ \dot A^q }\leq \|f\|_{ \dot A^p} \text{ for all } f\in  \dot A^p({\mathbb T}).
nodes.label: lem:P

nodes.name: Algebra inequality in Wiener spaces
nodes.statement:
Let $s\in \{0\}\cup[1,\infty)$ be a fixed parameter and $f,g\in \dot A^s({\mathbb T})$, then, due to the convexity of $x^s$ in this range,
\begin{equation} \|fg\|_{\dot{A}^s}\leq 2^{s-1}\left\|f\|_{\dot A^s}\|g\|_{\dot A^0}+\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|g\|_{\dot A^s}\right)\leq  2^{s}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^s}\|g\|_{\dot{A}^s},
\end{equation}
while, as a consequence of subadditivity of $x^s$, for $s\in (0,1)$, we have 
\[
	\|fg\|_{\dot{A}^s}\leq 2\|f\|_{\dot A^s}\|g\|_{\dot A^s}.
\]
assumptions: $s\in \{0\}\cup[1,\infty)$ be a fixed parameter and $f,g\in \dot A^s({\mathbb T})$
conclusions: \|fg\|_{\dot{A}^s}\leq 2\|f\|_{\dot A^s}\|g\|_{\dot A^s}.

nodes.name: Interpolation inequality in Wiener spaces
conclusions: \|f\|_{\dot{A}^{s\theta}}\leq \|f\|_{\dot A^0}^{1-\theta}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^{s}}^{\theta}\quad \mbox{for all }\quad 0<\theta<1.

nodes.name: Interpolation inequality (interpolation)
nodes.statement: \|f\|_{\dot{A}^{s\theta}}\leq \|f\|_{\dot A^0}^{1-\theta}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^{s}}^{\theta}\quad \mbox{for all }\quad 0<\theta<1.
nodes.label: interpolation

nodes.name: Thin film system with linear equation of state
nodes.statement_short: System (1) with $\sigma(s)=1-s$, with initial and boundary conditions.

nodes.name: Film height equation (7a)
nodes.statement:
{2}
	\partial_t h &=-\partial_x \left[ -\frac{h^2}{2}\partial_x\Gamma-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}h^3\partial_x h + \frac{\mathcal{S}}{3}h^3\partial_x^3h+\mathcal{A}\frac{\partial_x h}{h} \right],\; &&\mbox{in}\quad \Omega_T

nodes.name: Surfactant equation (7b)
nodes.statement: \partial_t \Gamma &=- \partial_x \left[\Gamma \left(-h \partial_x \Gamma-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2} h^2 \partial_x h +\frac{\mathcal{S}}{2} h^2 \partial_x^3 h + \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2} \frac{\partial_x h }{h^{2}}\right)-\mathcal{D}\partial_x \Gamma \right],\;&&\mbox{in}\quad \Omega_T,

nodes.name: Boundary conditions (eq:boundary)
nodes.statement: \partial_x h =\partial_x \Gamma=0, \quad \mathcal{S}\partial_x^3 f =0 \qquad \mbox{for all}\quad x\in \partial \Omega.
nodes.label: eq:boundary

nodes.name: Equivalence of the interval problem and the periodic problem on the torus
nodes.statement:
The problem is posed on a spatial interval $\Omega=(0,L)$ with the above lateral boundary conditions. However, without lossing generality, instead of considering an interval and no-flux boundary conditions, we are going to consider periodic solutions  $h,\Gamma$ of \eqref{eq:systemA} on a flat torus ${\mathbb T}$ (which can be identified with $[-\pi,\pi)$). This generalization actually simplifies our approach and it was already used in \cite{BG18} for similar problems. Let us explain why our formulation in the flat torus is actually equivalent to the original problem posed on the interval $(0,L)$. If $(h_0,\Gamma_0)$ are the initial data on an interval $\overline \Omega=[0,L]$ satisfying the boundary conditions \eqref{eq:boundary}, we set
	\[
	\bar h_0(x):= h_0(|x|) ,\quad 	\bar \Gamma_0(x):=\Gamma_0(|x|)\qquad \mbox{for}\quad x\in [-L,L].
	\]
		In view of the symmetry of \eqref{eq:systemA}, the evenness of initial data is preserved and any solution of \eqref{eq:systemA} on $[0,L]$ with initial data $(h_0,\Gamma_0)$ satisfying the boundary conditions \eqref{eq:boundary}, can be identified with the corresponding solution to even initial data $(\bar h_0, \bar \Gamma_0)$ on the periodic cell $[-L,L]$ restricted to the half-domain $[0,L]$. In the sequel we drop the bar notation and consider periodic solutions of \eqref{eq:systemA} defined on ${\mathbb T}$ with initial conditions 
\[
h(0,x)=h_0(x)\quad \mbox{and}\quad \Gamma(0,x)=\Gamma_0(x)\qquad \mbox{for all} \quad x\in {\mathbb T},
\]
where $h_0,\Gamma_0$ are given periodic functions.
nodes.statement_short: By even extension of the data, the no-flux problem on $(0,L)$ is equivalent to a periodic problem on the torus.

nodes.name: Proof of conservation of mass
nodes.statement: It follows immediately from the structure of the equations \eqref{eq:systemA} that the initial mass is preserved in time:
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the divergence (conservation) form of the equations.

nodes.name: Conservation of mass
nodes.statement:
Let $(h,\Gamma)$ be a solution of \eqref{eq:systemA} on a time interval $[0,T)$, then
\[
	\int_{{\mathbb T}} h(t,x)\,dx =	\int_{{\mathbb T}} h_0(x)\,dx\quad\mbox{and}\quad \int_{{\mathbb T}} \Gamma(t,x)\,dx =	\int_{{\mathbb T}} \Gamma_0(x)\,dx\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\in[0,T).
\]
assumptions: $(h,\Gamma)$ be a solution of \eqref{eq:systemA} on a time interval $[0,T)$
conclusions: \int_{{\mathbb T}} h(t,x)\,dx =	\int_{{\mathbb T}} h_0(x)\,dx\quad\mbox{and}\quad \int_{{\mathbb T}} \Gamma(t,x)\,dx =	\int_{{\mathbb T}} \Gamma_0(x)\,dx\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\in[0,T).

nodes.name: Mean initial height and concentration $h_\sharp$, $\Gamma_\sharp$
nodes.statement:
If $(h_0,\Gamma_0)$ are nonnegative bounded initial data, we set 
 $$
 h_\sharp=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb T} h_0(x)dx\quad\mbox{and}\quad \Gamma_\sharp=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb T} \Gamma_0(x)dx.
 $$

nodes.name: Mean values are a steady state
nodes.statement: The constants $h_\sharp$ and $\Gamma_\sharp$ represent the mean of the initial data and they are a steady state of the system \eqref{eq:systemA}.
conclusions: they are a steady state of the system \eqref{eq:systemA}

nodes.name: Deviation unknowns $f$, $\Theta$
nodes.statement:
For this purpose, we define new unknowns
\begin{equation} f=h-h_\sharp,\quad \Theta=\Gamma-\Gamma_\sharp,
\end{equation}
which have zero mean.

nodes.name: New unknowns (newunknown)
nodes.statement: f=h-h_\sharp,\quad \Theta=\Gamma-\Gamma_\sharp,
nodes.label: newunknown

nodes.name: Perturbation system around the flat equilibrium
nodes.statement_short: Linear part plus nonlinearities $N_1,\dots,N_8$ for the deviations $(f,\Theta)$ from the flat state.

nodes.name: Perturbation equation for $f$ (10a)
nodes.statement:
{2}
\partial_t f-\frac{h_\sharp^2}{2}\partial_x^2 \Theta +\left(\frac{\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}h_\sharp^3\right)\partial_x^2 f+\frac{\mathcal{S}}{3}h_\sharp^3\partial_x^4 f&=\sum_{j=1}^4 N_j,\; &&\mbox{in}\quad (0,T)\times {\mathbb T}

nodes.name: Perturbation equation for $\Theta$ (10b)
nodes.statement: \partial_t \Theta -\left(h_\sharp\Gamma_\sharp+\mathcal{D}\right)\partial_x^2\Theta+\left(\frac{3\mathcal{A}\Gamma_\sharp}{2h_\sharp^2}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2\right) \partial_x^2f+\frac{\mathcal{S}}{2}\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2 \partial_x^4f &= \sum_{j=5}^8 N_j,\;&& \mbox{in}\quad (0,T)\times {\mathbb T}

nodes.name: Nonlinear terms $N_1,\dots,N_8$
nodes.statement:
The nonlinear terms $N_i$, $i=1,\dots,8,$ on the right hand side of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} are defined as
\begin{align*}
N_1&=\partial_x\left[\left(\frac{f^2}{2}+fh_\sharp\right)\partial_x \Theta\right],\\
N_2&=\partial_x \left[\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}\left(3h_\sharp^2 f+3f^2h_\sharp+f^3\right)\partial_x f\right],\\
N_3&=-\partial_x \left[\frac{\mathcal{S}}{3}\left(3h_\sharp^2 f+3f^2h_\sharp+f^3\right)\partial_x^3 f\right],\\
N_4&=\partial_x \left[\mathcal{A}\frac{f}{h_\sharp^2(1+\frac{f}{h_\sharp})}\partial_x f \right],\\
N_5&=\partial_x\left[\left(\Gamma_\sharp f+\Theta h_\sharp+\Theta f\right)\partial_x \Theta\right],\\
N_6&=\partial_x\left[\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\left(\Gamma_\sharp f^2+2\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp f+\Theta h_\sharp^2+\Theta f^2+2\Theta h_\sharp f\right)\partial_x f\right],\\
N_7&=-\partial_x\left[\frac{\mathcal{S}}{2}\left(\Gamma_\sharp f^2+2\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp f+\Theta h_\sharp^2+\Theta f^2+2\Theta h_\sharp f\right)\partial_x^3 f\right],\\
N_8&=\partial_x \left[\Theta \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^2} \frac{(f^2+2h_\sharp f)\partial_x f }{(h_\sharp+f)^{2}}+\Gamma_\sharp\frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^2} \frac{(f^2+2h_\sharp f)\partial_x f }{(h_\sharp+f)^{2}}-\Theta \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^2} \partial_x f \right]\\
&= \partial_x \left[ \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2}\frac{2f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+f^2\Gamma_\sharp-\Theta h_\sharp^2}{h_\sharp^2(f+h_\sharp)^2}\partial_x f\right].
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Explicit formulas for the eight nonlinear terms of the perturbation system.

nodes.name: Power series of $(1+r)^{-1}$, $(1+r)^{-2}$, $(1+r)^{-3}$
Series for $(1+r)^{-2}$ (taylor2)
nodes.statement: \frac{1}{\left(1+r\right)^2}&=\sum_{j=1}^\infty j(-1)^{j+1}r^{j-1},
nodes.label: eq:taylor2

nodes.name: Series for $(1+r)^{-3}$ (taylor3)
nodes.statement: \frac{1}{\left(1+r\right)^3}&=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j=2}^\infty j(j-1)(-1)^{j}r^{j-2}.
nodes.label: eq:taylor3

nodes.name: Series expansion of $N_4$
nodes.statement_short: Under $\|f\|_{\dot A^0}<h_\sharp$, $N_4$ expands as a convergent power series in $f/h_\sharp$.

nodes.name: Size restriction (restriction1)
nodes.statement: \|f\|_{L^\infty}\leq \|f\|_{\dot A^0}< h_\sharp,
nodes.label: restriction1

nodes.name: Expansion of $N_4$ (NL4)
nodes.statement: N_4&=\mathcal{A} \bigg{[}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp^2}\partial_x^2 f +\left(\frac{\partial_x f}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\right)\sum_{j=1}^\infty (-1)^{j+1}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1}-\frac{f}{h_\sharp^3}(\partial_x f)^2\sum_{j=1}^\infty j(-1)^{j+1}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1} \bigg{]}.
nodes.label: NL4

nodes.name: Series expansion of $N_8$
nodes.statement:
Similarly, invoking  \eqref{eq:taylor2} and \eqref{eq:taylor3} we have that
\begin{align}
N_8&=\partial_x \left[ \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2}\frac{2f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+f^2\Gamma_\sharp-\Theta h_\sharp^2}{h_\sharp^2(f+h_\sharp)^2}\partial_x f\right]\nonumber\\
&= \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^4}\left[\frac{2f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+f^2\Gamma_\sharp-\Theta h_\sharp^2}{\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}+1\right)^2}\partial_x^2 f+\frac{2\partial_x f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+2f\partial_x f\Gamma_\sharp-\partial_x \Theta h_\sharp^2}{\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}+1\right)^2}\partial_x f\right]\nonumber\\
&\quad- \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp^4}\left[\frac{2f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+f^2\Gamma_\sharp-\Theta h_\sharp^2}{\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}+1\right)^3}\frac{(\partial_x f)^2}{h_\sharp}\right]\nonumber\\
&=\frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^4}\left[\left(2f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+f^2\Gamma_\sharp-\Theta h_\sharp^2\right)\partial_x^2 f+\left(2\partial_x f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+2f\partial_x f\Gamma_\sharp-\partial_x \Theta h_\sharp^2\right)\partial_x f\right]\sum_{j=1}^\infty j(-1)^{j+1}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1}\nonumber\\
&\quad- \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp^4}\left[\left(2f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+f^2\Gamma_\sharp-\Theta h_\sharp^2\right)\frac{(\partial_x f)^2}{h_\sharp}\right]\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j=2}^\infty j(j-1)(-1)^{j}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-2}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $N_8$ expands as power series in $f/h_\sharp$ using the series for $(1+r)^{-2}$ and $(1+r)^{-3}$.

nodes.name: Expansion of $N_8$ (NL8)
nodes.statement:
N_8&=\partial_x \left[ \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2}\frac{2f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+f^2\Gamma_\sharp-\Theta h_\sharp^2}{h_\sharp^2(f+h_\sharp)^2}\partial_x f\right]\nonumber\\
&= \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^4}\left[\frac{2f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+f^2\Gamma_\sharp-\Theta h_\sharp^2}{\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}+1\right)^2}\partial_x^2 f+\frac{2\partial_x f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+2f\partial_x f\Gamma_\sharp-\partial_x \Theta h_\sharp^2}{\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}+1\right)^2}\partial_x f\right]\nonumber\\
&\quad- \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp^4}\left[\frac{2f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+f^2\Gamma_\sharp-\Theta h_\sharp^2}{\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}+1\right)^3}\frac{(\partial_x f)^2}{h_\sharp}\right]\nonumber\\
&=\frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^4}\left[\left(2f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+f^2\Gamma_\sharp-\Theta h_\sharp^2\right)\partial_x^2 f+\left(2\partial_x f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+2f\partial_x f\Gamma_\sharp-\partial_x \Theta h_\sharp^2\right)\partial_x f\right]\sum_{j=1}^\infty j(-1)^{j+1}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1}\nonumber\\
&\quad- \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp^4}\left[\left(2f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+f^2\Gamma_\sharp-\Theta h_\sharp^2\right)\frac{(\partial_x f)^2}{h_\sharp}\right]\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j=2}^\infty j(j-1)(-1)^{j}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-2}.
nodes.label: NL8

nodes.name: Positive gravity, van der Waals and diffusion constants
nodes.statement: In what follows the constants $\mathcal G,\mathcal A,$ representing the gravitational and van der Waals forces as well as the diffusion coefficient $\mathcal D$ are assumed to be strictly positive.

nodes.name: Weak solution
nodes.statement_short: Weak formulation of the perturbation system with test functions $(\phi,\psi)$; defines $\zeta$ and $\partial_x^{-1}$.
nodes.label: defi1

nodes.name: Energy functional $\mathscr{E}^r_s$
Energy functional (energy)
nodes.statement: \mathscr{E}^r_{s}(f,\Theta):[0,T) \to [0,\infty),\qquad \mathscr{E}^r_{s}(f,\Theta)(t):=\|f(t)\|_{\dot{A}^r}+\|\Theta(t)\|_{\dot{A}^s}.
nodes.label: energy

nodes.name: Functions $\Lambda_1,\Lambda_2$ and constants $\mathfrak{C}_1,\mathfrak{C}_2$
nodes.statement_short: Explicit coefficient functions $\Lambda_1,\Lambda_2$ and dissipation constants $\mathfrak C_1,\mathfrak C_2$ for the gravity-driven case.

nodes.name: $\Lambda_1$ (eq:Lambda_1)
nodes.statement:
\Lambda_1(t)&:= h_\sharp+\frac{19h_\sharp^2\mathcal{ G}}{3}+ \frac{\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp^2}\left(1-\frac{\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}\bigg{[}2+\left(1-\frac{\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1} \bigg{]}+\Gamma_\sharp\nonumber \\ 
&\quad+\mathcal{G}\left(4\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp +5h_\sharp^2\right)+\frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^3}\left(1-\frac{\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-2}\Big\{7\Gamma_\sharp + \frac{3}{2}h_\sharp + \left(1-\frac{\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}4\Gamma_\sharp\Big\} ,
nodes.label: eq:Lambda_1

nodes.name: $\Lambda_2$ (eq:Lambda_2)
nodes.statement: \Lambda_2(t)&:=\frac{13}{2}h_\sharp+2\Gamma_\sharp+\mathcal{G}h_\sharp^2+\frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^3}\left(1-\frac{\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-2}\frac{h_\sharp}{2} \,,
nodes.label: eq:Lambda_2

nodes.name: $\mathfrak C_1$ (constant1)
nodes.statement: \mathfrak{C}_1&:=\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}h_\sharp^3-\frac{\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp}-\left|\frac{3\mathcal{A}\Gamma_\sharp}{2h_\sharp^2}-\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\right|,
nodes.label: constant1

nodes.name: $\mathfrak C_2$ (constant2)
nodes.statement: \mathfrak{C}_2&:=h_\sharp \Gamma_\sharp+\mathcal{D}-\frac{h_\sharp^2}{2}.
nodes.label: constant2

nodes.name: Global existence for $\mathcal{S}=0$
nodes.statement:
Let $f_0\in \dot A^0({\mathbb T}), \Theta_0\in \dot A^0({\mathbb T})$ be nontrivial  initial data for \eqref{eq:systemlinearized}
such that
$$
\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}.
$$
Assume that $\mathfrak{C}_1,\mathfrak{C}_2>0$. If
\begin{align*}
\gamma_1:=\mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(0)\mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)&>0,\\
\gamma_2:=\mathfrak{C}_2-\Lambda_2(0)\mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)&>0,
\end{align*}
then there exists at least one global solution $(f,\Theta)$ of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} in the sense of Definition \ref{defi1} with regularity
\begin{align*}
(f,\Theta)\in &\Big(L^{\frac{2}{r}}\left(0,T;W^{r,\infty}({\mathbb T})\right)\cap L^1\left(0,T;C^{1+\alpha}({\mathbb T})\right) \cap L^2(0,T;H^2({\mathbb T}))\Big)^2,
\end{align*}
for any $r\in[0,2), \alpha\in[0,\frac{1}{2})$ and $T>0$. Moreover, the weak solution satisfies the following exponential decay:
$$
\|f(t)\|_{L^\infty}+\|\Theta(t)\|_{L^\infty}\leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)e^{-\delta t},
$$
where 
\begin{equation} \delta=\min\{\gamma_1,\gamma_2\}>0.
\end{equation}
Furthermore, if the solution $(f,\Theta)$ satisfies the regularity
$$
(f,\Theta)\in \left(L^1\left(0,T;\dot{A}^2({\mathbb T})\right)\right)^2,
$$
then the weak solution is unique.
assumptions: $f_0\in \dot A^0({\mathbb T}), \Theta_0\in \dot A^0({\mathbb T})$ be nontrivial  initial data for \eqref{eq:systemlinearized}
conclusions: there exists at least one global solution $(f,\Theta)$ of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} in the sense of Definition \ref{defi1}
\|f(t)\|_{L^\infty}+\|\Theta(t)\|_{L^\infty}\leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)e^{-\delta t},
the weak solution is unique
nodes.statement_short: For medium-size Wiener-algebra data with explicit smallness conditions, the gravity-driven system has a global weak solution decaying exponentially; unique under extra regularity.

nodes.statement: \delta=\min\{\gamma_1,\gamma_2\}>0.

nodes.name: Positivity of initial data
nodes.statement:
The condition $
\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}
$ in Theorem \ref{global1} implies in particular that
\[
	\|f\|_{L^\infty}<\|f_0\|_{\dot A^0}<h_\sharp\quad\mbox{and}\quad \|\Theta\|_{L^\infty}<\|\Theta_0\|_{\dot A^0}<\Gamma_\sharp.
\]
This corresponds to a positivity condition of $h_0$ and $\Gamma_0$ and ensures that \eqref{restriction1} is initially satisfied.

nodes.name: Highly oscillating initial data
nodes.statement:
Note that the size restriction is explicitly computable and that the initial data do not need to be small in Sobolev spaces (one should compare the results in this paper with the global result in \cite{bruellwell}). In particular, we prove the existence global weak solutions and their decay towards the flat state for highly oscillating initial data. Let us further explain this with an explicit example. Consider the case where van der Waals forces are neglected, that is $\mathcal A=0$ and set $\mathcal G=\mathcal D=1$. We choose the initial data $(h_0,\Gamma_0)$ to be
$$
h_0(x)=1+\mu\sin(1000x)\quad \mbox{and}\quad \Gamma_0(x)=\frac{1}{2}+\mu\cos(1000x),
$$
for $0<\mu< \frac{1}{4}$. Then, 
$$
h_\sharp=1,\quad\Gamma_\sharp=\frac{1}{2},\quad\mathscr{E}^0_0(h_0-h_\sharp,\Gamma_0-\Gamma_\sharp)=2\mu,
$$
and the constants $\mathfrak{C}_1,\mathfrak{C}_2,\Lambda_1(0),$ and $\Lambda_2(0)$ are given by
$$
\mathfrak{C}_1=\frac{1}{12},\quad\mathfrak{C}_2=1,\quad \Lambda_1(0)= \frac{89}{6},\quad \Lambda_2(0)=\frac{17}{2}.
$$
Then, for $\mu<\frac{1}{356}\sim 0.003$, this family of initial data satisfies the hypotheses and Theorem~\ref{global1} guarantees the existence of a global weak solution $(h,\Gamma)$ corresponding to the initial data $(h_0,\Gamma_0)$. Moreover the solution decays exponentially towards the flat equilibrium and
\[
\|h(t)-h_\sharp\|_{L^\infty}+\|\Gamma-\Gamma_\sharp\|_{L^\infty}\leq 2\mu e^{-\delta t},
\]
where $\delta =\frac{1}{12}-\frac{89}{3}\mu$. Furthermore, observe that
$$
\|h_0\|_{\dot{C}^1}=\|\Gamma_0\|_{\dot{C}^1}=O(1) \quad \mbox{while}\quad \|h_0\|_{H^2}=\|\Gamma_0\|_{H^2}=O(10^3).
$$
nodes.statement_short: Explicit oscillating data $h_0=1+\mu\sin(1000x)$, $\Gamma_0=1/2+\mu\cos(1000x)$ satisfy Theorem 1 for $\mu<1/356$ despite large $H^2$ norm.

nodes.name: Constants $\Lambda_3$ and $\mathfrak{C}_3$
$\Lambda_3$ (eq:Lambda_3)
nodes.statement: \Lambda_3&:=\frac{\mathcal{S}}{2} (14h_\sharp\Gamma_\sharp +4h_\sharp^2)+\frac{19}{3}\mathcal{S}h_\sharp^2,
nodes.label: eq:Lambda_3

nodes.name: $\mathfrak C_3$ (constant3)
nodes.statement: \mathfrak{C}_3&:=\frac{\mathcal{S}}{3}h_\sharp^3-\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2\frac{\mathcal{S}}{2} .
nodes.label: constant3

nodes.name: Global existence for $\mathcal{S}>0$
nodes.statement:
Let $f_0\in \dot A^0({\mathbb T}), \Theta_0\in \dot A^0({\mathbb T})$ be nontrivial initial data for \eqref{eq:systemlinearized}
such that
$$
\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}.
$$
Assume that $\mathfrak{C}_1,\mathfrak{C}_2,\mathfrak{C}_3>0$. If
\begin{align*}
\gamma_1:=\mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(0)\mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)&>0,\\
\gamma_2:=\mathfrak{C}_2-\left(\Lambda_2(0)+\frac{\mathcal{S}h_\sharp^2}{2}\right)\mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)&>0,\\
\gamma_3:=\mathfrak{C}_3-\Lambda_3\mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)&>0,
\end{align*}
then there exists at least one global solution $(f,\Theta)$ of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} in the sense of Definition \ref{defi1} with regularity
\begin{align*}
f\in & L^\frac{4}{s}\left(0,T; W^{s,\infty}({\mathbb T})\right)\cap L^{1}\left(0,T;C^{3+\alpha}({\mathbb T})\right) \cap L^2\left(0,T;H^2({\mathbb T})\right),\quad s\in[0,4),\\
\Theta\in & L^\frac{4}{r}\left(0,T; W^{r,\infty}({\mathbb T})\right)\cap L^{1}\left(0,T;C^{1+\alpha}({\mathbb T})\right)\cap L^2\left(0,T;H^1({\mathbb T})\right),\quad r\in[0,2)
\end{align*}
for any $T$ and $0\leq\alpha<\frac{1}{2}$. Moreover, the weak solutions satisfies the following exponential decay:
$$
\|f(t)\|_{L^\infty}+\|\Theta(t)\|_{L^\infty}\leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)e^{-\delta t},
$$
where 
\begin{equation} \delta=\min\{\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\gamma_3\}>0.
\end{equation}
Furthermore, if the solution $(f,\Theta)$ satisfies the regularity
$$
(f,\Theta)\in L^1\left(0,T;\dot{A}^4({\mathbb T})\right)\times L^1\left(0,T;\dot{A}^2({\mathbb T})\right),
$$
then the weak solution is unique.
assumptions: $f_0\in \dot A^0({\mathbb T}), \Theta_0\in \dot A^0({\mathbb T})$ be nontrivial initial data for \eqref{eq:systemlinearized}
conclusions: there exists at least one global solution $(f,\Theta)$ of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} in the sense of Definition \ref{defi1}
\|f(t)\|_{L^\infty}+\|\Theta(t)\|_{L^\infty}\leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)e^{-\delta t},
the weak solution is unique
nodes.statement_short: Capillary-driven analogue of Theorem 1: global weak solutions with exponential decay under explicit size conditions; unique under extra regularity.

assumptions: $f_0\in \dot A^0({\mathbb T}), \Theta_0\in \dot A^0({\mathbb T})$ be nontrivial initial data for \eqref{eq:systemlinearized}
conclusions: there exists at least one global solution $(f,\Theta)$ of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} in the sense of Definition \ref{defi1}

nodes.statement: \delta=\min\{\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\gamma_3\}>0.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1 (gravity driven case)
nodes.statement:
Let us start by outlining the steps of the proof. First, we provide in Subsection \ref{ss:e} some \emph{a priori} estimates of a solution $(f,\Theta)\in \left(C^1(0,T;\dot A^0({\mathbb T}))\right)^2$ of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized}. Under the assumptions on the initial data in Theorem \ref{global1}, which in particular require that
\[
	\mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\},
\] 
we will show that the solution $(f,\Theta)$ preserves this estimate, that is
$$
\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}\quad\mbox{for all}\quad 0<t<T.
$$
Notice that the above inequality  implies that
$$
\|f(t)\|_{\dot A^0}\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}<h_\sharp \quad\mbox{for all}\quad 0<t<T,
$$
$$
\|\Theta(t)\|_{\dot A^0}\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}<\Gamma_\sharp \quad\mbox{for all}\quad 0<t<T.
$$
Hence, the positivity conditions for $h$ and $\Gamma$, 
$$
\|f(t)\|_{L^\infty}\leq \|f(t)\|_{\dot A^0} < h_\sharp,\quad \|\Theta(t)\|_{L^\infty}\leq \|\Theta(t)\|_{\dot A^0}<\Gamma_\sharp 
$$
are preserved for all $t\in [0,T)$. Then we obtain that, for small enough initial energy $\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)$, the following inequality holds:
$$
\frac{d}{dt} \mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)+\delta \mathscr{E}^2_2(f,\Theta)(t)\leq 0
$$
for some $\delta>0$ dependent on the initial data.
This inequality implies that a local solution $(f,\Theta)$ can not leave a ball in $(L^\infty((0,T); \dot A^0({\mathbb T}))\cap L^1(0,T;\dot A^2({\mathbb T})))^2$; thus, there is no finite time singularity in these functional spaces. 
In Subsection \ref{ss:gl} we implement a standard Galerkin approximation argument to prove the existence of global weak solutions. The existence of a classical local solution of the Galerkin approximated sytem is guaranteed by the Picard--Lindel\"of Theorem.  These approximated solutions $(f_M,\Theta_M)_{M\in {\mathbb N}}$ are analytic. In particular, they satisfy 
$$
(f_M,\Theta_M)\in \left(C^1([0,T_M); \dot A^0({\mathbb T}))\right)^2,
$$ where $T_M>0$ denotes the maximal time of existence of $(f_M,\Theta_M)$. The \emph{a priori} estimates from before ensure the \emph{global} existence of the approximated solutions and provide the necessary \emph{a priori} bounds in order to use compactness arguments and pass to the limit $M\to \infty$, which yields a global weak solution of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} in the sense of Definition \ref{defi1}. 
Now, let $(f_M,\Theta_M)$ be such approximate solution corresponding to the initial data $(f_0,\Theta_0)$, which satisfy the hypothesis of Theorem \ref{global1}, then, in view of the Poincar\'e-like inequality in \eqref{lem:P}, we see that
$\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)$ is a Lyapunov functional, \emph{i.e.}, that
$$
\frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)+\delta \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(0)\leq 0 \qquad \mbox{for all}\quad 0<t<\infty.
$$
The latter implies the exponential decay towards the equilibrium $(f^*,\Theta^*)=(0,0)$ for the global weak solution (see Subsection \ref{ss:decay}). Eventually, in Subsection \ref{ss:unique} it is shown that a global weak solution in 
$$
\left(L^1(0,T;\dot A^2({\mathbb T}))\right)^2
$$ is unique.


\medskip

\subsection{\emph{A priori} estimates in $\dot A^0({\mathbb T})$:} Let $T\in (0,\infty]$ and 
$$
(f,\Theta)\in \left( C^1([0,T), \dot A({\mathbb T}))\right)^2
$$ 
be a local solution of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} with initial data 
$$
(f_0,\Theta_0)\in \left(\dot A({\mathbb T})\right)^2
$$ 
satisfying the condition
\[
	\mathcal{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}.
\]
By continuity there exists $0<t_*\leq T$ such that the above estimate is satisfied  on $[0,t_*)$, that is
\begin{equation} \mathcal{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}\qquad\mbox{for all}\quad t\in [0,t_*).
\end{equation}
Let us moreover assume that $t_*$ is the maximal time such that \eqref{eq:t} holds true on $[0,t_*)$. Hence, either
\begin{equation} \mathcal{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t_*)=\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}
\end{equation}
or $t_*=T$.
Notice that the restriction \eqref{restriction1} holds true on the time interval $[0,t_*)$. In the following let $t\in [0,t_*)$.
We compute
\begin{align*}
\partial_t|\hat{f}(k)| &=\frac{\text{Re}\left(\bar{\hat{f}}(k)\partial_t\hat{f}(k)\right)}{|\hat{f}(k)|},
\end{align*}
so, using that $\mathcal{S}=0$,
\begin{align}
\frac{d}{dt}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq\frac{h_\sharp^2}{2}\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2} +\left(\frac{\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}h_\sharp^3\right)\| f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\|N_1\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_2\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_4\|_{\dot A^0} ,\\
\frac{d}{dt}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq-\left(h_\sharp \Gamma_\sharp+\mathcal{D}\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\left|\frac{3\mathcal{A}\Gamma_\sharp}{2h_\sharp^2}-\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\right| \|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\|N_5\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_6\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_8\|_{\dot A^0} \end{align}
We recall that
\begin{align*}
\widehat{uv}(k)=\sum_{j\in{\mathbb Z}}\hat{u}(j)\hat{v}(k-j)
\end{align*}
and by the hypothesis of the theorem
\[
	\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\leq h_\sharp,\qquad \|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\leq \Gamma_\sharp.
\]
Using the algebra property of the Wiener space $A^s({\mathbb T})$, \emph{i.e.}
$$
\|fg\|_{\dot{A}^s}\leq 2^{s}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})}\|g\|_{\dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})},\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad \, f,g\in \dot A^s({\mathbb T}),\quad s\in{\mathbb N},
$$
together with the interpolation inequality
$$
\|f\|_{\dot{A}^{s\theta}({\mathbb T})}\leq \|f\|_{\dot A^0({\mathbb T})}^{1-\theta}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})}^{\theta},\quad \mbox{for all} \quad 0<\theta<1,\quad s\geq0,
$$
the contribution of the nonlinear terms $N_k$, $k=1,2,$ and $4$, can be estimated as
\begin{align*}
\|N_1\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq \left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^2}{2}+\|f\|_{\dot A^0}h_\sharp\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\left(\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}+\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}h_\sharp\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}\\
&\leq \left(\frac{3}{2}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}h_\sharp+h_\sharp\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+h_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\
&\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta) \frac{5}{2}h_\sharp\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+h_\sharp\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\,,
\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
\|N_2\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}\bigg[\left(3h_\sharp^2 \|f\|_{\dot A^0}+3\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^2h_\sharp+\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^3\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\
&\quad+\left(3h_\sharp^2 \|f\|_{A^1}+6\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}h_\sharp+3\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^2\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}\bigg]\\
&\leq\frac{19h_\sharp^2\mathcal{ G}}{3} \|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\
&\leq \frac{19h_\sharp^2\mathcal{ G}}{3} \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\,,
\end{align*}
and
\begin{align*}
\|N_4\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq\mathcal{A} \bigg{[}\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}}{h_\sharp} +\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\right)\sum_{j=1}^\infty\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1}\\
&\quad +\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\sum_{j=1}^\infty j\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1} \bigg{]}\\
&\leq\mathcal{A} \bigg{[}\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}}{h_\sharp} +\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\right)\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}\\
&\quad+\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-2} \bigg{]}\\
&\leq\mathcal{A} \frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}}{h_\sharp}\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}\bigg{[}2+\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1} \bigg{]}\\
&\leq \mathcal{A} \frac{\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)}{h_\sharp}\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}}{h_\sharp}\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}\bigg{[}2+\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1} \bigg{]} ,
\end{align*}
where we used the convergence of the geometric series $\sum_{j=1}^\infty r^{j-1}$ for $|r|<1$, and
\[
	\sum_{j=1}^\infty jr^{j-1}=\partial_r \sum_{j=1}^{\infty}r^j = \frac{1}{(1-r)^2},\qquad |r|<1.
\]
Similarly,
the nonlinear terms $N_j$, $j=5,6,$ and $8$ are bounded by
\begin{align*}
\|N_5\|_{\dot A^0}

&\leq \left(\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}+\left(4h_\sharp+\Gamma_\sharp\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0} \right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+ \Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\
&\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\left(4h_\sharp+2\Gamma_\sharp \right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+ \Gamma_\sharp\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\,,\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
\|N_6\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq\mathcal{G}\left[\left(4\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp \|f\|_{\dot A^0}+4\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}h_\sharp^2\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+h_\sharp^2\left(\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\right)\right]\\
&\leq \mathcal{G}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\left[\left(4\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp +4h_\sharp^2\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+h_\sharp^2\left(\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\right)\right]\,,
\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
\|N_8\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^4}\bigg{[}\left(3\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0} h_\sharp^2\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\
&\quad+\left(4\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\frac{h_\sharp^2}{2}\left[\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\right] \right)\bigg{]}\sum_{j=1}^\infty j\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1}\nonumber\\
&\quad+ \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp^3}\left[2\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\right]\sum_{j=2}^\infty j(j-1)\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-2}\\
&\leq \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^3}\bigg{[}\left(3\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\Gamma_\sharp+\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0} h_\sharp\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\
&\quad+\left(4\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\frac{h_\sharp}{2}\left[\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\right] \right)\bigg{]}\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-2}\nonumber\\
&\quad+ \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp^3}\left[2\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\right]\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-3}.
\end{align*}
Grouping terms, we find that
\begin{align*}
\|N_8\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^3}\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-2}\Big\{7\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot A^2} + \frac{1}{2}h_\sharp[\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot A^2}+{\frac{h_\sharp}{2}}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^2}] \\
  &\qquad + h_\sharp \|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot A^2}+ \left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}4\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot A^2}\Big\}\\
&\leq \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^3}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-2}\Big\{7\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^2} + \frac{1}{2}h_\sharp[\|f\|_{\dot A^2}+{\frac{h_\sharp}{2}}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^2}] \\
  &\qquad + h_\sharp \|f\|_{\dot A^2}+ \left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}4\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^2}\Big\}.
\end{align*}



We recall the definition \eqref{constant1} and \eqref{constant2}, then we add equations \eqref{eq:1} and \eqref{eq:2}, use the previous estimates for $N_j$, $j=1,2,4,5,6,$ and 8 and  obtain that
\begin{align} \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)&\leq -\left(\mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(t)\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\right)\|f(t)\|_{\dot{A}^2}-\left(\mathfrak{C}_2-\Lambda_2(t)\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\right)\|\Theta(t)\|_{\dot{A}^2}
\end{align}
 for $t\in[0,t_*)$,
with $\Lambda_1$ and $\Lambda_2$ defined in \eqref{eq:Lambda_1} and \eqref{eq:Lambda_2},  respectively. 
Using the hypothesis of the Theorem \ref{global1}, we have that
\begin{align*}
\frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\bigg{|}_{t=0}&<0,
\end{align*}
so, there exists a time $0<t_0\leq t_*$ such that
\begin{equation} \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\in [0,t_0].
\end{equation}
Let us assume that $t_0$ is the maximal times such that \eqref{eq:estimate} holds true on $[0,t_0]$
We want to propagate this decay for all times, that is, we aim to show that $t_0=t_*$, which in turn implies that $t_0=t_*=T$, by \eqref{eq:O1}. Let us emphasize that $\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)$ for $t\in [0,t_0]$ guarantees that
\begin{equation} \Lambda_j(t)\leq \Lambda_j(0),\qquad j=1,2 \qquad\mbox{for all}\quad t\in [0,t_0].
\end{equation}
Thereby, for any $t\in [0,t_0]$ we have that
$$
\mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(t)\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\geq \mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(0)\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)=\gamma_1>0,
$$
$$
\mathfrak{C}_2-\Lambda_2(t)\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\geq \mathfrak{C}_2-\Lambda_2(0)\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)=\gamma_2>0.
$$
In particular, we obtain that 
\begin{align*}
\frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)&< 0\qquad\mbox{for all}\quad t\in [0,t_0).
\end{align*}
Assume that $t_0<t_*$. By continuity, we deduce that $\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t_0)=\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(0)$, but this implies that, again, 
\begin{align*}
\frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\bigg{|}_{t=t_0}&\leq 0,
\end{align*}
and that contradicts the assumption $t_0<t_*$. Thus, we have shown that in fact
\begin{equation} \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\in[0,t_*)
\end{equation}
and thereby $t_*=T$,
in view of \eqref{eq:O1}.
Then,
\begin{equation} \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq -\gamma \mathscr{E}^2_2(f,\Theta)(t)\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\in[0,T),
\end{equation}
where $\delta:=\min\{\gamma_1,\gamma_2\}$. Eventually, the energy estimate for the gravity driven equation ($\mathcal S =0$) reads
\[
	\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)+\delta\int_0^t \mathscr{E}^2_2(f,\Theta)(\tau)\, d\tau \leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)
\]
and
\[
	\int_0^t \|\partial_t f(\tau)\|_{\dot A^0}+\|\partial_t \Theta(\tau)\|_{\dot A^0}\, d\tau\leq c,
\]
for all $t\in[0,T)$, where $c>0$ is a constant depending on the initial data.

\medskip


\subsection{Existence of global weak solutions} We use a standard Galerkin approximation to obtain in the limit a global weak solution of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} where surface tension effects are neglected, \emph{i.~e.} $\mathcal{S}=0$. Let us fix $M\in {\mathbb Z}^+$. Set
\[
	f_M(t,x):=\sum_{|k|\leq M} \hat f(t,k)e^{ikx}\qquad \mbox{and}\qquad 	\Theta_M(t,x):=\sum_{|k|\leq M} \hat \theta(t,k)e^{ikx}
\]
and the initial data
\[
	f_M(0,x):=\sum_{|k|\leq M} \hat f_0(k)e^{ikx}\qquad \mbox{and}\qquad 	\Theta_M(0,x):=\sum_{|k|\leq M} \hat \theta_0(k)e^{ikx}
\]
to coincide with the Fourier truncation of the $f_0$ and $\Theta_0$, respectively. Recall that the convergence of the Fourier series of the initial data is guaranteed by the assumption that $f_0,\Theta_0\in \dot A^0({\mathbb T})$. We consider the Galerkin approximated problems:
	\begin{alignat*}{2}
	\partial_t f_M-\frac{h_\sharp^2}{2}\partial_x^2 \Theta_M +\left(\frac{\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}h_\sharp^3\right)\partial_x^2 f_M+\frac{\mathcal{S}}{3}h_\sharp^3\partial_x^4 f_M&=\sum_{j=1,2,4} N_j^M,\; && \text{ in }(0,T)\times{\mathbb T}\\
	\partial_t \Theta_M -\left(h_\sharp\Gamma_\sharp+\mathcal{D}\right)\partial_x^2\Theta_M+\left(\frac{3\mathcal{A}\Gamma_\sharp}{2h_\sharp^2}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2\right) \partial_x^2f_M+\frac{\mathcal{S}}{2}\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2 \partial_x^4f_M &= \sum_{j=5,6,8} N_j^M,\;&& \text{ in }(0,T)\times{\mathbb T}
	\end{alignat*}
where the nonlinearities $N_j^M$ are given by

\begin{align*}
N_1^M&=\partial_x P_M\left[\left(\frac{f^2}{2}+fh_\sharp\right)\partial_x \Theta\right],\\
N_2^M&=\partial_x P_M \left[\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}\left(3h_\sharp^2 f+3f^2h_\sharp+f^3\right)\partial_x f\right],\\
N_4^M&=\mathcal{A} P_M \bigg{[}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp^2}\partial_x^2 f +\left(\frac{\partial_x f}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\right)\sum_{j=1}^M (-1)^{j+1}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1}-\frac{f}{h_\sharp^3}(\partial_x f)^2\sum_{j=1}^M j(-1)^{j+1}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1} \bigg{]},\\
N_5^M&=\partial_x P_M\left[\left(\Gamma_\sharp f+\Theta h_\sharp+\Theta f\right)\partial_x \Theta\right],\\
N_6^M&=\partial_x P_M\left[\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\left(\Gamma_\sharp f^2+2\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp f+\Theta h_\sharp^2+\Theta f^2+2\Theta h_\sharp f\right)\partial_x f\right],\\
N_8^M&=\frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^4} P_M\left[\left(2f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+f^2\Gamma_\sharp-\Theta h_\sharp^2\right)\partial_x^2 f+\left(2\partial_x f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+2f\partial_x f\Gamma_\sharp-\partial_x \Theta h_\sharp^2\right)\partial_x f\right]\sum_{j=1}^M j(-1)^{j+1}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1}\nonumber\\
&\quad- \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp^4} P_M\left[\left(2f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+f^2\Gamma_\sharp-\Theta h_\sharp^2\right)\frac{(\partial_x f)^2}{h_\sharp}\right]\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j=2}^M j(j-1)(-1)^{j}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-2}.
\end{align*}
Here, the operator $P_M$ denotes the Fourier truncation operator
\[
	P_M g(x)=\sum_{|k|\leq M} \hat g(k)e^{ikx}\qquad\mbox{for any}\quad g\in \dot A^0({\mathbb T}).
\]
The Picard--Lindel\"of Theorem ensures the existence of classical solutions 
\[
f_M,\Theta_M\in C^1([0,T_M);C^\infty({\mathbb T})),
\]
 where $T_M>0$ is the maximal existence time.  Furthermore, the approximated problems provide the same \emph{a priori} bounds as in the previous sections.  Consequently the Galerkin solutions  $(f_M,\Theta_M)_{M\in {\mathbb N}}$ exist globally and for any $T>0$ we have the bounds:
\begin{equation} (f_M,\Theta_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}} \quad \mbox{is uniformly bounded in}\quad \left( L^\infty\left(0,T;\dot A^0({\mathbb T})\right)\cap L^1\left(0,T; \dot A^2({\mathbb T}) \right)\right)^2
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation} (\partial_t f_M,\partial_t\Theta_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}} \quad \mbox{is uniformly bounded in}\quad \left( L^1\left(0,T; \dot A^0({\mathbb T}) \right)\right)^2.
\end{equation}
Following the lines in \cite{BG18}, the above uniform regularities of the Galerkin approximations $(f_M,\Theta_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}} $ guarantee the existence of a weakly convergent subsequences (not relabeled) such that 
\begin{align*}
(f_M,\Theta_M)\overset{*}{\rightharpoonup}  (f,\Theta)\text {  in $\left(L^{\infty}(0,T;L^\infty({\mathbb T}))\right)^2$}.
\end{align*}
Similarly, using interpolation in Wiener spaces, the finite measure of the spatial domain and the fact that $\dot A^r({\mathbb T})\subset \dot W^{r,\infty}({\mathbb T})$ for any $r\geq 0$, we obtain the existence of a subsequence (not relabeled), such that
\begin{align} (f_M,\Theta_M)\rightharpoonup  (f,\Theta)\text {   in $\left(L^{\frac{2}{r}}(0,T;\dot W^{r,p}({\mathbb T}))\right)^2$},\qquad 0\leq r<2,\;\;1\leq p<\infty.
\end{align}
From the previous fact we can infer that actually
$$
(f,\Theta) \in \left(L^{\frac{2}{r}}(0,T;\dot W^{r,\infty}({\mathbb T}))\right)^2,\qquad 0\leq r<2.
$$
Furthermore \eqref{boundedness}, \eqref{boundednesst} imply that
$$
	(f_M,\Theta_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}} \text{ is uniformly bounded in }   \left(L^2(0,T;H^{1}({\mathbb T}))\right)^2,
$$
which is due to $\dot A^s({\mathbb T})\subset \dot H^s({\mathbb T})$ for any $s \geq 0$ and an interpolation inequality for fractional Sobolev spaces. Eventually, as a consequence of \eqref{boundedness},\eqref{boundednesst} and a  compactness argument as in \cite[Corollary 4]{simon1986compact}, we obtain (up to a subsequence) that
$$
(f_M,\Theta_M)\rightarrow (f,\Theta)\qquad \text{ in $\left(L^1(0,T;{C}^{1+s}({\mathbb T}))\right)^2$}, \quad \,0\leq s<\frac{1}{2}.
$$
Passing to the limit in the weak formulation of the Galerkin approximation yields the existence of a global weak solution of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} in the sense of Definition \ref{defi1}.

\subsection{Exponential trend to equilibrium} Using \eqref{eq:energyE} and the definition of $\delta>0$ in \eqref{delta}, we have that
\begin{align} \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)\leq -\delta\mathscr{E}^2_2(f_M,\Theta_M)(t) \qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\geq0.
\end{align}
Using the Poincar\'e-like inequality \eqref{lem:P}, we also conclude that 
$$
\frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)\leq -\delta\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t) \qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\geq0,
$$ 
 which in turn implies the exponential decay towards the equilibrium:
\[
\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)e^{-\delta t}\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\geq0.
\]
Using \eqref{eq:Linf1} and the lower semi-continuity of the weak$-*$ convergence, we have that
\begin{equation*}
\|f(t)\|_{L^\infty({\mathbb T})}+\|\Theta(t)\|_{L^\infty({\mathbb T})}\leq \liminf_{k\to \infty}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)\leq 	\mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)e^{-\delta t}.
\end{equation*}

\subsection{Uniqueness} The proof follows a standard contradiction argument. For the sake of brevity, we only sketch the idea. Assume that there exist two different solutions $(f_1,\Theta_1)$ and $(f_2,\Theta_2)$ starting from the same initial data 
$$
(f_0,\Theta_0)\in \left(\dot A^0({\mathbb T})\right)^2.
$$ 
Assume also that these solutions satisfy 
$$
(f_i,\Theta_i)\in \left( L^{1}(0,T;\dot A^2({\mathbb T}))\right)^2.
$$ Using the smallness of the initial data, the same estimates as in Subsection \ref{ss:e} yield that
\begin{multline*}
\frac{d}{dt}\left(\|f_1-f_2\|_{\dot A^0}+\|\Theta_1-\Theta_2\|_{\dot A^0}\right)\\
\leq C\left[\|f_1-f_2\|_{\dot A^0}+\|\Theta_1-\Theta_2\|_{\dot A^0}\right]\left(\|f_1\|_{\dot A^2}+\|f_2\|_{\dot A^2}+\|\Theta_1\|_{\dot A^2}+\|\Theta_2\|_{\dot A^2}+1\right).
\end{multline*} 

Now the statement is a consequence of Gronwall's  inequality and the fact that $(f_1,\Theta_1)(0)=(f_2,\Theta_2)(0)$.

nodes.statement_short: A priori $\dot A^0$ energy estimates via Wiener-algebra bounds on the nonlinearities, then Galerkin approximation and compactness. A continuity argument propagates the decay of $\mathscr{E}^0_0$ for all times.

nodes.name: Outline of the proof
nodes.statement:
Let us start by outlining the steps of the proof. First, we provide in Subsection \ref{ss:e} some \emph{a priori} estimates of a solution $(f,\Theta)\in \left(C^1(0,T;\dot A^0({\mathbb T}))\right)^2$ of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized}. Under the assumptions on the initial data in Theorem \ref{global1}, which in particular require that
\[
	\mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\},
\] 
we will show that the solution $(f,\Theta)$ preserves this estimate, that is
$$
\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}\quad\mbox{for all}\quad 0<t<T.
$$
Notice that the above inequality  implies that
$$
\|f(t)\|_{\dot A^0}\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}<h_\sharp \quad\mbox{for all}\quad 0<t<T,
$$
$$
\|\Theta(t)\|_{\dot A^0}\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}<\Gamma_\sharp \quad\mbox{for all}\quad 0<t<T.
$$
Hence, the positivity conditions for $h$ and $\Gamma$, 
$$
\|f(t)\|_{L^\infty}\leq \|f(t)\|_{\dot A^0} < h_\sharp,\quad \|\Theta(t)\|_{L^\infty}\leq \|\Theta(t)\|_{\dot A^0}<\Gamma_\sharp 
$$
are preserved for all $t\in [0,T)$. Then we obtain that, for small enough initial energy $\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)$, the following inequality holds:
$$
\frac{d}{dt} \mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)+\delta \mathscr{E}^2_2(f,\Theta)(t)\leq 0
$$
for some $\delta>0$ dependent on the initial data.
This inequality implies that a local solution $(f,\Theta)$ can not leave a ball in $(L^\infty((0,T); \dot A^0({\mathbb T}))\cap L^1(0,T;\dot A^2({\mathbb T})))^2$; thus, there is no finite time singularity in these functional spaces. 
In Subsection \ref{ss:gl} we implement a standard Galerkin approximation argument to prove the existence of global weak solutions. The existence of a classical local solution of the Galerkin approximated sytem is guaranteed by the Picard--Lindel\"of Theorem.  These approximated solutions $(f_M,\Theta_M)_{M\in {\mathbb N}}$ are analytic. In particular, they satisfy 
$$
(f_M,\Theta_M)\in \left(C^1([0,T_M); \dot A^0({\mathbb T}))\right)^2,
$$ where $T_M>0$ denotes the maximal time of existence of $(f_M,\Theta_M)$. The \emph{a priori} estimates from before ensure the \emph{global} existence of the approximated solutions and provide the necessary \emph{a priori} bounds in order to use compactness arguments and pass to the limit $M\to \infty$, which yields a global weak solution of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} in the sense of Definition \ref{defi1}. 
Now, let $(f_M,\Theta_M)$ be such approximate solution corresponding to the initial data $(f_0,\Theta_0)$, which satisfy the hypothesis of Theorem \ref{global1}, then, in view of the Poincar\'e-like inequality in \eqref{lem:P}, we see that
$\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)$ is a Lyapunov functional, \emph{i.e.}, that
$$
\frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)+\delta \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(0)\leq 0 \qquad \mbox{for all}\quad 0<t<\infty.
$$
The latter implies the exponential decay towards the equilibrium $(f^*,\Theta^*)=(0,0)$ for the global weak solution (see Subsection \ref{ss:decay}). Eventually, in Subsection \ref{ss:unique} it is shown that a global weak solution in 
$$
\left(L^1(0,T;\dot A^2({\mathbb T}))\right)^2
$$ is unique.

nodes.name: A priori estimates in $\dot A^0$
nodes.statement:
\subsection{\emph{A priori} estimates in $\dot A^0({\mathbb T})$:} Let $T\in (0,\infty]$ and 
$$
(f,\Theta)\in \left( C^1([0,T), \dot A({\mathbb T}))\right)^2
$$ 
be a local solution of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} with initial data 
$$
(f_0,\Theta_0)\in \left(\dot A({\mathbb T})\right)^2
$$ 
satisfying the condition
\[
	\mathcal{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}.
\]
By continuity there exists $0<t_*\leq T$ such that the above estimate is satisfied  on $[0,t_*)$, that is
\begin{equation} \mathcal{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}\qquad\mbox{for all}\quad t\in [0,t_*).
\end{equation}
Let us moreover assume that $t_*$ is the maximal time such that \eqref{eq:t} holds true on $[0,t_*)$. Hence, either
\begin{equation} \mathcal{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t_*)=\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}
\end{equation}
or $t_*=T$.
Notice that the restriction \eqref{restriction1} holds true on the time interval $[0,t_*)$. In the following let $t\in [0,t_*)$.
We compute
\begin{align*}
\partial_t|\hat{f}(k)| &=\frac{\text{Re}\left(\bar{\hat{f}}(k)\partial_t\hat{f}(k)\right)}{|\hat{f}(k)|},
\end{align*}
so, using that $\mathcal{S}=0$,
\begin{align}
\frac{d}{dt}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq\frac{h_\sharp^2}{2}\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2} +\left(\frac{\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}h_\sharp^3\right)\| f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\|N_1\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_2\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_4\|_{\dot A^0} ,\\
\frac{d}{dt}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq-\left(h_\sharp \Gamma_\sharp+\mathcal{D}\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\left|\frac{3\mathcal{A}\Gamma_\sharp}{2h_\sharp^2}-\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\right| \|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\|N_5\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_6\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_8\|_{\dot A^0} \end{align}
We recall that
\begin{align*}
\widehat{uv}(k)=\sum_{j\in{\mathbb Z}}\hat{u}(j)\hat{v}(k-j)
\end{align*}
and by the hypothesis of the theorem
\[
	\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\leq h_\sharp,\qquad \|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\leq \Gamma_\sharp.
\]
Using the algebra property of the Wiener space $A^s({\mathbb T})$, \emph{i.e.}
$$
\|fg\|_{\dot{A}^s}\leq 2^{s}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})}\|g\|_{\dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})},\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad \, f,g\in \dot A^s({\mathbb T}),\quad s\in{\mathbb N},
$$
together with the interpolation inequality
$$
\|f\|_{\dot{A}^{s\theta}({\mathbb T})}\leq \|f\|_{\dot A^0({\mathbb T})}^{1-\theta}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})}^{\theta},\quad \mbox{for all} \quad 0<\theta<1,\quad s\geq0,
$$
the contribution of the nonlinear terms $N_k$, $k=1,2,$ and $4$, can be estimated as
\begin{align*}
\|N_1\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq \left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^2}{2}+\|f\|_{\dot A^0}h_\sharp\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\left(\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}+\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}h_\sharp\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}\\
&\leq \left(\frac{3}{2}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}h_\sharp+h_\sharp\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+h_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\
&\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta) \frac{5}{2}h_\sharp\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+h_\sharp\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\,,
\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
\|N_2\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}\bigg[\left(3h_\sharp^2 \|f\|_{\dot A^0}+3\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^2h_\sharp+\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^3\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\
&\quad+\left(3h_\sharp^2 \|f\|_{A^1}+6\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}h_\sharp+3\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^2\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}\bigg]\\
&\leq\frac{19h_\sharp^2\mathcal{ G}}{3} \|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\
&\leq \frac{19h_\sharp^2\mathcal{ G}}{3} \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\,,
\end{align*}
and
\begin{align*}
\|N_4\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq\mathcal{A} \bigg{[}\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}}{h_\sharp} +\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\right)\sum_{j=1}^\infty\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1}\\
&\quad +\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\sum_{j=1}^\infty j\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1} \bigg{]}\\
&\leq\mathcal{A} \bigg{[}\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}}{h_\sharp} +\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\right)\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}\\
&\quad+\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-2} \bigg{]}\\
&\leq\mathcal{A} \frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}}{h_\sharp}\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}\bigg{[}2+\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1} \bigg{]}\\
&\leq \mathcal{A} \frac{\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)}{h_\sharp}\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}}{h_\sharp}\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}\bigg{[}2+\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1} \bigg{]} ,
\end{align*}
where we used the convergence of the geometric series $\sum_{j=1}^\infty r^{j-1}$ for $|r|<1$, and
\[
	\sum_{j=1}^\infty jr^{j-1}=\partial_r \sum_{j=1}^{\infty}r^j = \frac{1}{(1-r)^2},\qquad |r|<1.
\]
Similarly,
the nonlinear terms $N_j$, $j=5,6,$ and $8$ are bounded by
\begin{align*}
\|N_5\|_{\dot A^0}

&\leq \left(\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}+\left(4h_\sharp+\Gamma_\sharp\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0} \right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+ \Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\
&\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\left(4h_\sharp+2\Gamma_\sharp \right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+ \Gamma_\sharp\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\,,\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
\|N_6\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq\mathcal{G}\left[\left(4\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp \|f\|_{\dot A^0}+4\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}h_\sharp^2\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+h_\sharp^2\left(\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\right)\right]\\
&\leq \mathcal{G}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\left[\left(4\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp +4h_\sharp^2\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+h_\sharp^2\left(\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\right)\right]\,,
\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
\|N_8\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^4}\bigg{[}\left(3\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0} h_\sharp^2\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\
&\quad+\left(4\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\frac{h_\sharp^2}{2}\left[\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\right] \right)\bigg{]}\sum_{j=1}^\infty j\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1}\nonumber\\
&\quad+ \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp^3}\left[2\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\right]\sum_{j=2}^\infty j(j-1)\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-2}\\
&\leq \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^3}\bigg{[}\left(3\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\Gamma_\sharp+\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0} h_\sharp\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\
&\quad+\left(4\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\frac{h_\sharp}{2}\left[\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\right] \right)\bigg{]}\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-2}\nonumber\\
&\quad+ \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp^3}\left[2\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\right]\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-3}.
\end{align*}
Grouping terms, we find that
\begin{align*}
\|N_8\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^3}\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-2}\Big\{7\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot A^2} + \frac{1}{2}h_\sharp[\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot A^2}+{\frac{h_\sharp}{2}}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^2}] \\
  &\qquad + h_\sharp \|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot A^2}+ \left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}4\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot A^2}\Big\}\\
&\leq \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^3}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-2}\Big\{7\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^2} + \frac{1}{2}h_\sharp[\|f\|_{\dot A^2}+{\frac{h_\sharp}{2}}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^2}] \\
  &\qquad + h_\sharp \|f\|_{\dot A^2}+ \left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}4\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^2}\Big\}.
\end{align*}



We recall the definition \eqref{constant1} and \eqref{constant2}, then we add equations \eqref{eq:1} and \eqref{eq:2}, use the previous estimates for $N_j$, $j=1,2,4,5,6,$ and 8 and  obtain that
\begin{align} \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)&\leq -\left(\mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(t)\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\right)\|f(t)\|_{\dot{A}^2}-\left(\mathfrak{C}_2-\Lambda_2(t)\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\right)\|\Theta(t)\|_{\dot{A}^2}
\end{align}
 for $t\in[0,t_*)$,
with $\Lambda_1$ and $\Lambda_2$ defined in \eqref{eq:Lambda_1} and \eqref{eq:Lambda_2},  respectively. 
Using the hypothesis of the Theorem \ref{global1}, we have that
\begin{align*}
\frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\bigg{|}_{t=0}&<0,
\end{align*}
so, there exists a time $0<t_0\leq t_*$ such that
\begin{equation} \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\in [0,t_0].
\end{equation}
Let us assume that $t_0$ is the maximal times such that \eqref{eq:estimate} holds true on $[0,t_0]$
We want to propagate this decay for all times, that is, we aim to show that $t_0=t_*$, which in turn implies that $t_0=t_*=T$, by \eqref{eq:O1}. Let us emphasize that $\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)$ for $t\in [0,t_0]$ guarantees that
\begin{equation} \Lambda_j(t)\leq \Lambda_j(0),\qquad j=1,2 \qquad\mbox{for all}\quad t\in [0,t_0].
\end{equation}
Thereby, for any $t\in [0,t_0]$ we have that
$$
\mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(t)\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\geq \mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(0)\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)=\gamma_1>0,
$$
$$
\mathfrak{C}_2-\Lambda_2(t)\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\geq \mathfrak{C}_2-\Lambda_2(0)\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)=\gamma_2>0.
$$
In particular, we obtain that 
\begin{align*}
\frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)&< 0\qquad\mbox{for all}\quad t\in [0,t_0).
\end{align*}
Assume that $t_0<t_*$. By continuity, we deduce that $\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t_0)=\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(0)$, but this implies that, again, 
\begin{align*}
\frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\bigg{|}_{t=t_0}&\leq 0,
\end{align*}
and that contradicts the assumption $t_0<t_*$. Thus, we have shown that in fact
\begin{equation} \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\in[0,t_*)
\end{equation}
and thereby $t_*=T$,
in view of \eqref{eq:O1}.
Then,
\begin{equation} \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq -\gamma \mathscr{E}^2_2(f,\Theta)(t)\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\in[0,T),
\end{equation}
where $\delta:=\min\{\gamma_1,\gamma_2\}$. Eventually, the energy estimate for the gravity driven equation ($\mathcal S =0$) reads
\[
	\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)+\delta\int_0^t \mathscr{E}^2_2(f,\Theta)(\tau)\, d\tau \leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)
\]
and
\[
	\int_0^t \|\partial_t f(\tau)\|_{\dot A^0}+\|\partial_t \Theta(\tau)\|_{\dot A^0}\, d\tau\leq c,
\]
for all $t\in[0,T)$, where $c>0$ is a constant depending on the initial data.

nodes.name: A priori estimates in $\dot A^0$ for $\mathcal S>0$
nodes.statement:
\subsection{\emph{A priori} estimates in $\dot A^0({\mathbb T})$:} 
To perform our energy estimates let us assume that there exists a local solution 
$$
(f,\Theta)\in \left(C^1([0,T), \dot A^0({\mathbb T})) \right)^2
$$ 
of the fourth-order system \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} where $\mathcal{S}>0$, corresponding to initial data $(f_0,\Theta_0)$, satisfying 
\[
	\mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}.
\]

Similar as before, we have that
\begin{align}
\frac{d}{dt}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq\frac{h_\sharp^2}{2}\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2} +\left(\frac{\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}h_\sharp^3\right)\| f\|_{\dot{A}^2} - \frac{\mathcal{S}}{3}h_\sharp^3\|f\|_{\dot A^4}+\sum_{j=1}^4\|N_j\|_{\dot A^0} ,\\
\frac{d}{dt}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq-\left(h_\sharp \Gamma_\sharp+\mathcal{D}\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\left|\frac{3\mathcal{A}\Gamma_\sharp}{2h_\sharp^2}-\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\right|\|f\|_{\dot A^2}+\frac{\mathcal{S}}{2}h_\sharp^2\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^4} +\sum_{j=5}^8\|N_j\|_{\dot A^0}. \end{align}
Keeping in mind the definitions of $\mathfrak{C_i}$, $i=1,2,3,$ in \eqref{constant1}, \eqref{constant2}, and \eqref{constant3}, we take the sum of the two inequalities above and obtain that

$$
\frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)+\mathfrak{C}_1\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\mathfrak{C}_2\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\mathfrak{C}_3\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}\leq \sum_{j=1}^8\|N_j\|_{\dot A^0}.
$$
Recalling \eqref{eq:energyE}, we have that
\begin{align*}
\frac{d}{dt}&\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)+\mathfrak{C}_3\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}\\
&\leq \|N_3\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_7\|_{\dot A^0} -\left(\mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(t)\mathscr{E}^0_0(t)\right)\|f(t)\|_{\dot{A}^2}-\left(\mathfrak{C}_2-\Lambda_2(t)\mathscr{E}^0_0(t)\right)\|\Theta(t)\|_{\dot{A}^2},
\end{align*}
where $\Lambda_1$ and $\Lambda_2$ are defined in \eqref{eq:Lambda_1} and \eqref{eq:Lambda_2}, respectively.
Thus we are left to estimate the remaining terms $\|N_3\|_{\dot A^0}$ and $\|N_7\|_{\dot A^0}$. Similarly as before, using the interpolation inequality in Wiener spaces, we estimate
\begin{align*}
\|N_3\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq \frac{19}{3}\mathcal{S}h_\sharp^2\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4},
\end{align*}
and
\begin{align*}
\|N_7\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq \frac{\mathcal{S}}{2}\left(6\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp \|f\|_{\dot A^0}+h_\sharp^2\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}\\
&\quad +\frac{\mathcal{S}}{2}\left(8\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp \|f\|_{A^1}+4\|\Theta\|_{A^1}h_\sharp^2\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^3}.
\end{align*}
Note that by Young's inequality, we have that
$$
\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^3}\leq \|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^{\frac{1}{4}}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}^{\frac{3}{4}}\leq\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}\left(\frac{1}{4\varepsilon}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}+\frac{3\varepsilon}{4}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}\right), 
$$
for any $\varepsilon>0$. In particular, as $\Theta$ and $f$ are nonzero (provided the initial data are nontrivial), we can take
$$
\varepsilon=\frac{\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)}{\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}}.
$$
Thus,
$$
\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^3}\leq\frac{\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}^2}{4\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}+\frac{3\mathscr{E}_0^0}{4}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}\leq \frac{\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)}{4}+\frac{3\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)}{4}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}. 
$$
Then, we conclude that
	\[
		\|N_7\|_{\dot A^0}\leq \frac{\mathcal{S}}{2}\left( (14h_\sharp\Gamma_\sharp +4h_\sharp^2)\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta) \|f\|_{\dot A^4}+h_\sharp^2\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta) \|\Theta\|_{\dot A^2}\right).
	\]
Using \eqref{eq:Lambda_3}, we can group terms as follows:
\begin{align*}
\frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)&\leq -\left(\mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(t)\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\right)\|f(t)\|_{\dot{A}^2}-\left(\mathfrak{C}_2-\left(\Lambda_2(t)+\frac{\mathcal{S}h_\sharp^2}{2}\right)\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\right)\|\Theta(t)\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\
&\quad-\left(\mathfrak{C}_3-\Lambda_3\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\right)\|f(t)\|_{\dot{A}^4}.
\end{align*}
Repeating the argument from Section \ref{S:T1}, we conclude  that
\begin{equation} \mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)e^{-\delta t} 
\end{equation}
where $\delta$ is defined in \eqref{delta}. The energy estimate for the capillary driven thin film ($\mathcal S >0$) reads
\begin{equation*}
\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)+ \int_0^t\delta \mathscr{E}^4_2(f,\Theta)(\tau)\, d\tau \leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)
\end{equation*}
and
\[
\int_0^t \|\partial_t f(\tau)\|_{\dot A^0}+\|\partial_t \Theta(\tau)\|_{\dot A^0}\,d\tau \leq c,
\]
for all $t\in[0,T)$, where $c>0$ is a constant depending on the initial data.
nodes.statement_short: Energy inequality with the additional $\|f\|_{\dot A^4}$ dissipation and bounds on $N_3,N_7$.

nodes.statement:
Let $T\in (0,\infty]$ and 
$$

$$ 
be a local solution of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} with initial data

	\mathcal{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}.
\]

\begin{equation} \mathcal{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t_*)=\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}
\end{equation}
or $t_*=T$.
Notice that the restriction \eqref{restriction1} holds true on the time interval $[0,t_*)$. In the following let $t\in [0,t_*)$.

nodes.name: Bounds for $N_1$, $N_2$, $N_4$
nodes.statement:
Using the algebra property of the Wiener space $A^s({\mathbb T})$, \emph{i.e.}
$$
\|fg\|_{\dot{A}^s}\leq 2^{s}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})}\|g\|_{\dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})},\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad \, f,g\in \dot A^s({\mathbb T}),\quad s\in{\mathbb N},
$$
together with the interpolation inequality
$$
\|f\|_{\dot{A}^{s\theta}({\mathbb T})}\leq \|f\|_{\dot A^0({\mathbb T})}^{1-\theta}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})}^{\theta},\quad \mbox{for all} \quad 0<\theta<1,\quad s\geq0,
$$
the contribution of the nonlinear terms $N_k$, $k=1,2,$ and $4$, can be estimated as
\begin{align*}
\|N_1\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq \left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^2}{2}+\|f\|_{\dot A^0}h_\sharp\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\left(\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}+\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}h_\sharp\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}\\
&\leq \left(\frac{3}{2}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}h_\sharp+h_\sharp\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+h_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\
&\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta) \frac{5}{2}h_\sharp\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+h_\sharp\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\,,
\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
\|N_2\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}\bigg[\left(3h_\sharp^2 \|f\|_{\dot A^0}+3\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^2h_\sharp+\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^3\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\
&\quad+\left(3h_\sharp^2 \|f\|_{A^1}+6\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}h_\sharp+3\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^2\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}\bigg]\\
&\leq\frac{19h_\sharp^2\mathcal{ G}}{3} \|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\
&\leq \frac{19h_\sharp^2\mathcal{ G}}{3} \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\,,
\end{align*}
and
\begin{align*}
\|N_4\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq\mathcal{A} \bigg{[}\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}}{h_\sharp} +\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\right)\sum_{j=1}^\infty\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1}\\
&\quad +\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\sum_{j=1}^\infty j\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1} \bigg{]}\\
&\leq\mathcal{A} \bigg{[}\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}}{h_\sharp} +\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\right)\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}\\
&\quad+\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-2} \bigg{]}\\
&\leq\mathcal{A} \frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}}{h_\sharp}\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}\bigg{[}2+\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1} \bigg{]}\\
&\leq \mathcal{A} \frac{\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)}{h_\sharp}\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}}{h_\sharp}\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}\bigg{[}2+\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1} \bigg{]} ,
\end{align*}
where we used the convergence of the geometric series $\sum_{j=1}^\infty r^{j-1}$ for $|r|<1$, and
\[
	\sum_{j=1}^\infty jr^{j-1}=\partial_r \sum_{j=1}^{\infty}r^j = \frac{1}{(1-r)^2},\qquad |r|<1.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Estimate $N_1,N_2,N_4$ by the algebra and interpolation inequalities and geometric series.

nodes.name: Bounds for $N_5$, $N_6$, $N_8$
nodes.statement_short: Estimate $N_5,N_6,N_8$ analogously.

nodes.name: Grouping terms in $N_8$
nodes.statement:
Grouping terms, we find that
\begin{align*}
\|N_8\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^3}\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-2}\Big\{7\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot A^2} + \frac{1}{2}h_\sharp[\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot A^2}+{\frac{h_\sharp}{2}}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^2}] \\
  &\qquad + h_\sharp \|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot A^2}+ \left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}4\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot A^2}\Big\}\\
&\leq \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^3}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-2}\Big\{7\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^2} + \frac{1}{2}h_\sharp[\|f\|_{\dot A^2}+{\frac{h_\sharp}{2}}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^2}] \\
  &\qquad + h_\sharp \|f\|_{\dot A^2}+ \left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}4\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^2}\Big\}.
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Collect terms in the bound for $N_8$.
